summary: The 'gaia' version implements a multi-agent system using the SPADE framework. It successfully models the required agent roles (User, LLMProcessor, DataHandler, Analyzer, Institution, Recommendation, Admin, Monitoring), but many internal implementations are simplistic placeholders or keyword-based simulations for 'demonstration purposes'.

findings.description: Uses the SPADE framework to establish a robust asynchronous multi-agent communication environment.
findings.evidence: from spade.agent import Agent in agents/base_agent.py

findings.description: LLM processing is simulated using simple keyword matching instead of actual model calls, despite the presence of an API key placeholder.
findings.evidence: def extract_symptoms(self, text): ... keywords = ['fever', 'cough' ...] in agents/llm_processor_agent.py

findings.description: Lacks explicit data protection mechanisms; the system assumes a trusted environment without encryption or authentication logic for sensitive health data.
findings.evidence: No encryption or PII protection logic found in agents/health_data_handler_agent.py

findings.description: Satisfies the multi-agent requirement comprehensively with eight distinct agent types.

implementation_risks: Simulated logic may fail when encountering complex natural language input that doesn't match the simple keyword list.
